sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，一具女性遗体在加利福尼亚州的一个葡萄园中被发现。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她惨遭斩首，体内的血液也被排干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 凶手似乎费尽心机，试图掩盖她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，她一直被称为“简·多伊”（无名氏）。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 直到后来，侦探们终于查明了她的名字——艾达。

sentences.en: But, identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 然而，确认了她的身份，反而让这起离奇的谋杀案变得更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是“Casefile Presents”推出的全新系列节目，现已在各大播客平台上线。

sentences.en: This episode was originally released on Casefile's Patreon, Apple Premium, and Spotify Premium feeds as an early bonus for our paid subscribers.
sentences.zh: 本集最初作为给付费订阅者的早期福利，发布在Casefile的Patreon、Apple Premium和Spotify Premium频道上。

sentences.en: These episodes are designed to be slightly shorter, allowing us to cover a broader range of cases.
sentences.zh: 这些剧集篇幅稍短，旨在让我们能够涵盖更广泛的案件。

sentences.en: To receive these episodes early and ad-free, you can support Casefile on your preferred platform.
sentences.zh: 如需抢先收听无广告版剧集，您可以在您偏好的平台上支持Casefile。

sentences.en: The three-member Slayton family lived in a one-storey, two-bedroom duplex off Brunel Parkway in the Florida city of Lakeland.
sentences.zh: 斯莱顿一家三口住在佛罗里达州莱克兰市布鲁内尔大道旁的一栋单层双卧复式公寓里。

sentences.en: Single mum Linda slept in one bedroom, with her youngest son Tim in the other.
sentences.zh: 单亲妈妈琳达住在一间卧室，她最小的儿子蒂姆住在另一间。

sentences.en: Linda's oldest boy, 15-year-old Jeff, slept on a cot in the living room.
sentences.zh: 琳达的大儿子，15岁的杰夫，则睡在客厅的一张折叠床上。

sentences.en: It was early on Friday, September 4, 1981, when Jeff Slayton woke to a strange sound.
sentences.zh: 1981年9月4日，星期五清晨，杰夫·斯莱顿被一阵奇怪的声音惊醒。

sentences.en: It was the crackle of a police radio.
sentences.zh: 那是警用无线电的沙沙声。

sentences.en: Jeff quickly realised that several officers had gained access to his home and were quietly moving about.
sentences.zh: 杰夫很快意识到，几名警察已经进入了他家，正在悄无声息地走动。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: “怎么了？”

sentences.en: he asked.
sentences.zh: 他问道。

sentences.en: Jeff was told to get dressed and go outside.
sentences.zh: 警察让杰夫穿好衣服，去外面等候。

sentences.en: He did so, completely perplexed as to why the police were even there.
sentences.zh: 他照做了，完全不明白警察为什么会出现在家里。

sentences.en: The officers made sure he exited out the front door, away from his mother's bedroom.
sentences.zh: 警察特意让他从前门离开，避开了他母亲的卧室。

sentences.en: Jeff wandered out into the morning light and was immediately taken aback.
sentences.zh: 杰夫走到晨光中，顿时被眼前的景象惊呆了。

sentences.en: It seemed like every cop in Florida was standing outside his home, along with news crews and reporters.
sentences.zh: 仿佛佛罗里达州所有的警察都站在他家门外，还有新闻摄制组和记者。

sentences.en: Jeff spotted his auntie Judy among the crowd.
sentences.zh: 杰夫在人群中看到了他的朱迪阿姨。

sentences.en: Judy told Jeff that his mother had been murdered.
sentences.zh: 朱迪告诉杰夫，他母亲被谋杀了。

sentences.en: Shortly before Jeff woke up that day, Judy Butler arrived at the Slayton's apartment to have her regular Friday morning coffee with her older sister, Linda.
sentences.zh: 就在杰夫那天醒来前不久，朱迪·巴特勒来到斯莱顿家，准备和姐姐琳达像往常一样喝周五早晨的咖啡。

sentences.en: The sisters lived in the same government-owned complex, just three doors away from each other.
sentences.zh: 姐妹俩住在同一个政府公租房小区，相隔仅三户人家。

sentences.en: Judy knocked on Linda's front door several times and waited.
sentences.zh: 朱迪敲了几次琳达的前门，但无人应答。

sentences.en: When no one answered, she headed back home.
sentences.zh: 见没人开门，她便转身回家。

sentences.en: Along the way, she glanced over at Linda's bedroom window.
sentences.zh: 走在路上时，她瞥了一眼琳达的卧室窗户。

sentences.en: It was wide open and its screen had been removed.
sentences.zh: 窗户大开着，纱窗也不见了。

sentences.en: Judy went to examine it.
sentences.zh: 朱迪走过去查看。

sentences.en: Inside, Judy could see her sister's still figure sprawled across the bed, seemingly fast asleep.
sentences.zh: 透过窗户，朱迪看到姐姐的身体一动不动地横在床上，看起来像是睡得很沉。

sentences.en: But Judy thought it was strange that Linda was lying horizontally instead of vertically with her head on the pillow.
sentences.zh: 但朱迪觉得奇怪，琳达怎么是横着躺的，而不是头枕在枕头上纵向躺着。

sentences.en: As Judy processed the scene, she was suddenly hit with the realisation of what she was seeing and let out a blood-curdling scream.
sentences.zh: 当朱迪看清现场时，她突然意识到自己看到了什么，随即发出了一声撕心裂肺的尖叫。

sentences.en: A maintenance worker for the housing authority heard the scream and contacted police, who arrived soon after 8.35am.
sentences.zh: 住房管理局的一名维修工听到了尖叫声并报了警，警察在上午8点35分后不久赶到。

sentences.en: They observed 31-year-old Linda Slayton's body through her bedroom window.
sentences.zh: 他们透过卧室窗户观察了31岁的琳达·斯莱顿的遗体。

sentences.en: It was clear she was deceased.
sentences.zh: 很明显，她已经遇害了。

sentences.en: The officers wandered around the property looking for a way in, but all of the doors and every other window was locked.
sentences.zh: 警察在房子周围寻找入口，但所有的门和每一扇窗户都锁得严严实实。

sentences.en: They didn't want to disturb the scene by entering through Linda's bedroom window.
sentences.zh: 他们不想通过琳达的卧室窗户进入，以免破坏现场。

sentences.en: But Judy Butler was distraught.
sentences.zh: 但朱迪·巴特勒已经崩溃了。

sentences.en: Her nephews, Jeff and Tim, would be inside the apartment and she was scared they might have been hurt too.
sentences.zh: 她的两个侄子杰夫和蒂姆还在公寓里，她担心他们也可能受了伤。

sentences.en: Left with no other option and facing an urgent situation, officers climbed through the open window into Linda's bedroom.
sentences.zh: 别无选择且情况紧急，警察爬过那扇敞开的窗户进入了琳达的卧室。

sentences.en: The noise of their arrival woke Jeff Slayton in the living room.
sentences.zh: 他们进入时的动静惊醒了客厅里的杰夫·斯莱顿。

sentences.en: His younger brother, 12-year-old Tim, was asleep in the second bedroom.
sentences.zh: 他12岁的弟弟蒂姆正在第二间卧室熟睡。

sentences.en: You need to wake up, a policeman told a confused Tim.
sentences.zh: “你得起床了，”一名警察对困惑的蒂姆说。

sentences.en: Go outside with your brother.
sentences.zh: “跟你哥哥去外面。”

sentences.en: Tim wondered why the officer didn't mention his mother.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆纳闷警察为什么没提他母亲。

sentences.en: Still wearing his pyjamas, Tim headed towards the front door.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆穿着睡衣走向前门。

sentences.en: The door to his mother's room was closed, but when Tim walked by, it swung open as a police officer emerged.
sentences.zh: 母亲房间的门关着，但当蒂姆走过时，门开了，一名警察从里面走出来。

sentences.en: Tim caught a glimpse inside.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆瞥了一眼房间里面。

sentences.en: His mother's body lay awkwardly on the bed.
sentences.zh: 他母亲的遗体以一种扭曲的姿势躺在床上。

sentences.en: Her dress was bunched around her abdomen, exposing both her upper and lower naked body.
sentences.zh: 她的裙子堆在腹部周围，上半身和下半身都赤裸着。

sentences.en: Her underwear was on the floor and a wire was twisted around her bloodied neck.
sentences.zh: 她的内衣掉在地板上，一根铁丝缠在她血迹斑斑的脖子上。

sentences.en: It was a sight that Tim would never be able to erase from his mind.
sentences.zh: 这一幕成了蒂姆永远无法抹去的心理阴影。

sentences.en: 53-year-old Sergeant Edgar Pickett led the Lakeland Police Department's crime scene unit.
sentences.zh: 53岁的埃德加·皮克特警长负责莱克兰警察局的犯罪现场调查组。

sentences.en: He was a legendary fingerprint expert and only one year away from retirement when he was summoned to the Slayton's apartment.
sentences.zh: 他是一位传奇的指纹专家，距离退休仅剩一年，当时他被传唤到斯莱顿的公寓。

sentences.en: Upon arriving, a detective remarked to Sergeant Pickett, who was African American,
sentences.zh: 到达现场后，一名侦探对身为非裔美国人的皮克特警长说：

sentences.en: a black man don't have any business looking at a naked white woman.
sentences.zh: “黑人没资格看赤裸的白人女性。”

sentences.en: Despite his successful career and upstanding reputation, Pickett still faced prejudice on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 尽管职业生涯成功且声誉卓著，皮克特依然每天面临偏见。

sentences.en: Of the many deaths he'd attended, Pickett had never seen anyone treated as brutally as Linda Slayton.
sentences.zh: 在他处理过的众多死亡案件中，皮克特从未见过像琳达·斯莱顿这样惨遭毒手的受害者。

sentences.en: She had been sexually assaulted, then strangled to death with a wire coat hanger from her own closet, all while her two young sons slept close by.
sentences.zh: 她在两个年幼的儿子熟睡时，遭到了性侵，随后被衣柜里的金属衣架勒死。

sentences.en: Aside from the displaced window screen, everything else appeared to be in place.
sentences.zh: 除了被移位的纱窗外，其他一切看起来都井然有序。

sentences.en: Linda's purse was still in her room and her jewellery lay undisturbed in a box on her dresser.
sentences.zh: 琳达的钱包还在房间里，梳妆台盒子里的首饰也未被动过。

sentences.en: There were no overt signs of a struggle, indicating the altercation had taken place entirely on the bed.
sentences.zh: 现场没有明显的打斗痕迹，说明冲突完全发生在床上。

sentences.en: Sergeant Pickett examined the entire room for evidence.
sentences.zh: 皮克特警长检查了整个房间寻找证据。

sentences.en: Shoe prints were found on the carpet leading from the window to the closet.
sentences.zh: 地毯上发现了从窗户通往衣柜的鞋印。

sentences.en: Pickett also discovered a partial palm print on the windowsill.
sentences.zh: 皮克特还在窗台上发现了一个残缺的掌印。

sentences.en: It cemented the police's theory that Linda's killer had broken into her room, as opposed to being invited in.
sentences.zh: 这证实了警方的推测：琳达的凶手是破窗而入，而非受邀进入。

sentences.en: Linda's final movements were pieced together.
sentences.zh: 琳达生前的最后行踪被拼凑了出来。

sentences.en: She and her sons had only been living in the apartment for about two weeks.
sentences.zh: 她和儿子们搬进这间公寓才大约两周。

sentences.en: The previous afternoon of Thursday September 3,
sentences.zh: 前一天，9月3日星期四，

sentences.en: 15-year-old Jeff Slayton had arrived home to find there was nothing to eat.
sentences.zh: 15岁的杰夫·斯莱顿回到家，发现家里没吃的了。

sentences.en: The Slaytons lived in government housing and relied on welfare.
sentences.zh: 斯莱顿一家住在政府公租房，依靠救济金生活。

sentences.en: They didn't have much, but Jeff knew his mother loved her family and did the best she could.
sentences.zh: 他们虽然没什么钱，但杰夫知道母亲深爱这个家，并尽她所能照顾他们。

sentences.en: There could be two cans and a bag of flour in the cupboard, and Linda would still manage to make a feaSt.
sentences.zh: 哪怕橱柜里只有两罐头和一袋面粉，琳达也能设法做出一顿大餐。

sentences.en: Her single priority was caring for her boys.
sentences.zh: 她唯一的重心就是照顾好两个儿子。

sentences.en: Linda took Jeff and Tim out to the beach, parks and to concerts, with her goal always being to have fun.
sentences.zh: 琳达常带杰夫和蒂姆去海滩、公园和看演出，目标总是为了让他们开心。

sentences.en: Although she struggled to make ends meet and keep her sons in line,
sentences.zh: 尽管她难以维持生计并管教好儿子，

sentences.en: Linda maintained a positive and happy outlook on life.
sentences.zh: 琳达始终保持着积极乐观的生活态度。

sentences.en: When speaking with police, Jeff Slayton admitted to being somewhat rebellious and clashing with his mother.
sentences.zh: 在接受警方询问时，杰夫·斯莱顿承认自己有些叛逆，常与母亲发生冲突。

sentences.en: He maintained it was only ever typical teenage blow-ups and nothing serious.
sentences.zh: 但他坚称那只是典型的青春期争吵，没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: They'd had one such conflict on September 3, when Jeff became angry over the lack of food at home.
sentences.zh: 9月3日他们就发生过一次这样的冲突，当时杰夫因为家里没吃的而发火。

sentences.en: He left the apartment and rode his bike to his maternal grandparents' house.
sentences.zh: 他离开了公寓，骑车去了外祖父母家。

sentences.en: They fed him and dropped him back home at around 9.30 that night.
sentences.zh: 外祖父母喂饱了他，并在那天晚上9点半左右把他送回了家。

sentences.en: 12-year-old Tim Slayton had spent the latter part of the day at football practice and was given a ride home afterwards.
sentences.zh: 12岁的蒂姆·斯莱顿那天下午参加了足球训练，之后搭便车回家。

sentences.en: He arrived at around 8.30pm, shortly before his older brother returned.
sentences.zh: 他在晚上8点半左右到达，比他哥哥回来早一点。

sentences.en: Tim then attended a get-together at an apartment next door with his mother.
sentences.zh: 随后，蒂姆和母亲一起参加了隔壁公寓的一个聚会。

sentences.en: A small group inside were playing cards and Linda and Tim joined in.
sentences.zh: 屋里有一小群人在打牌，琳达和蒂姆也加入了。

sentences.en: At about 10 o'clock, Linda went back to her apartment to let Jeff know where she was, then returned to the card game.
sentences.zh: 大约10点钟，琳达回到自己的公寓告诉杰夫她在哪里，然后又回到了牌局。

sentences.en: She and Tim headed home at about 11.30pm.
sentences.zh: 她和蒂姆在晚上11点半左右回家。

sentences.en: Jeff was still up in the living room watching television.
sentences.zh: 杰夫当时还在客厅看电视。

sentences.en: Tim went to bed as Linda washed dishes in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆去睡觉了，琳达在厨房洗碗。

sentences.en: Jeff said that by now the tension between them had eased.
sentences.zh: 杰夫说，此时他们之间的紧张气氛已经缓和了。

sentences.en: As Linda passed him on the way to her room, he said,
sentences.zh: 当琳达去卧室经过他身边时，他说：

sentences.en: I love you, Mum.
sentences.zh: “我爱你，妈妈。”

sentences.en: I'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: “明天见。”

sentences.en: Linda replied, I love you, Jeff.
sentences.zh: 琳达回答说：“我也爱你，杰夫。”

sentences.en: Good night.
sentences.zh: “晚安。”

sentences.en: Jeff said he turned the TV off at around midnight, then fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 杰夫说他在午夜左右关掉电视，然后睡着了。

sentences.en: Though he described his 4-foot, 10-inch mother as weighing just 100 pounds soaking wet,
sentences.zh: 虽然他形容身高4英尺10英寸（约1.47米）的母亲体重只有100磅（约45公斤），

sentences.en: Jeff maintained she was tough and capable of fighting back against an attacker.
sentences.zh: 但杰夫坚称她很坚强，有能力反抗袭击者。

sentences.en: Yet, neither he nor Tim reported hearing anything amiss during the night.
sentences.zh: 然而，他和蒂姆都表示当晚没有听到任何异常动静。

sentences.en: Jeff insisted that if he knew his mother was in danger, he would have rushed to help.
sentences.zh: 杰夫坚称，如果他知道母亲有危险，他一定会冲过去帮忙。

sentences.en: Traces of semen found inside Linda formed the basis of a rape kit.
sentences.zh: 在琳达体内发现的精液痕迹成为了强奸取证的基础。

sentences.en: As forensic DNA analysis was still a few years away, investigators had to narrow down potential suspects using more traditional means.
sentences.zh: 由于当时法医DNA分析技术还需要几年才能普及，调查人员不得不通过更传统的方式缩小潜在嫌疑人范围。

sentences.en: Many people were questioned, including those at the car game Linda attended hours before she was killed, and other neighbours.
sentences.zh: 许多人都受到了盘问，包括琳达遇害前几小时参加牌局的人，以及其他邻居。

sentences.en: Police also spoke with a local construction worker named Bobby Dean who Linda had been dating.
sentences.zh: 警方还询问了一名琳达曾交往过的当地建筑工人，名叫鲍比·迪恩。

sentences.en: They discovered the couple had reportedly broken up two days before Linda was killed and that Linda had told others that Bobby was possessive of her.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这对情侣据称在琳达遇害前两天分手了，而且琳达曾告诉别人鲍比对她有很强的占有欲。

sentences.en: Bobby said he was at home with his sister and mother on the night of the murder.
sentences.zh: 鲍比说案发当晚他和母亲及姐姐在家。

sentences.en: They confirmed this, but couldn't be certain if he stayed home after they went to bed.
sentences.zh: 她们证实了这一点，但无法确定他在她们睡觉后是否一直待在家里。

sentences.en: Bobby agreed to take a polygraph teSt.
sentences.zh: 鲍比同意接受测谎仪测试。

sentences.en: Police also looked into Jeff and Tim's father, Frank Slayton.
sentences.zh: 警方还调查了杰夫和蒂姆的父亲，弗兰克·斯莱顿。

sentences.en: He was described by Linda's sister, Judy, as a mean, no-count scoundrel.
sentences.zh: 琳达的姐姐朱迪形容他是个卑鄙、一无是处的无赖。

sentences.en: Linda and Frank met as teenagers and had their two children young.
sentences.zh: 琳达和弗兰克在青少年时期相识，很早就有了两个孩子。

sentences.en: They'd married, wanting to provide their sons with a proper family experience.
sentences.zh: 他们结婚了，希望能给儿子们一个完整的家庭。

sentences.en: For years, the four of them had lived together in the neighbouring state of Alabama.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们一家四口一直住在邻近的阿拉巴马州。

sentences.en: But it hadn't been the happy family unit the young parents had hoped for.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有成为这对年轻父母所期望的幸福家庭。

sentences.en: Jeff and Tim both recalled times when their father had beaten their mother.
sentences.zh: 杰夫和蒂姆都记得父亲殴打母亲的场景。

sentences.en: Frank's violence escalated when he was drunk, which was often.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克喝醉后暴力倾向会升级，而他经常喝醉。

sentences.en: When Jeff was seven years old, he saw his father grab his mother by the throat, then press a gun to her head.
sentences.zh: 杰夫7岁时，曾亲眼看到父亲抓住母亲的喉咙，然后用枪顶着她的头。

sentences.en: Jeff intervened by pulling Frank away.
sentences.zh: 杰夫上前拉开了弗兰克。

sentences.en: He believed that if he hadn't done this, Frank could have pulled the trigger.
sentences.zh: 他相信如果自己没这么做，弗兰克可能会扣动扳机。

sentences.en: In mid-1981, after nine years of marriage, Linda had filed for divorce.
sentences.zh: 1981年中期，在九年婚姻后，琳达提出了离婚。

sentences.en: That was when she relocated to Lakeland with her sons for a fresh start.
sentences.zh: 那时她带着儿子们搬到了莱克兰，准备重新开始。

sentences.en: Given Frank Slayton's history of domestic violence and the sexual tone to Linda's murder, he became a strong suspect.
sentences.zh: 鉴于弗兰克·斯莱顿有家庭暴力史，且琳达的谋杀案带有性侵色彩，他成了重点嫌疑人。

sentences.en: Frank, who still lived in Alabama, insisted that he was at home when his ex-wife was killed.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克仍住在阿拉巴马州，他坚称前妻遇害时他在家。

sentences.en: After their mother's murder, Jeff and Tim Slayton went to live with their maternal grandparents and never set foot in their apartment again.
sentences.zh: 母亲遇害后，杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿搬去与外祖父母同住，再也没有踏进过那间公寓。

sentences.en: The boys referred to the unknown killer as the monster and lived in constant fear of him.
sentences.zh: 兄弟俩把那个未知的凶手称为“怪物”，并一直生活在对他的恐惧中。

sentences.en: It took time before they felt comfortable leaving their grandparents' house.
sentences.zh: 过了很久，他们才敢离开外祖父母家。

sentences.en: The local community shared the same anxieties, believing the person responsible was among them and would strike again.
sentences.zh: 当地社区也有同样的焦虑，认为凶手就在他们中间，而且还会再次作案。

sentences.en: The Slayton boys spent many nights sleeping in their grandparents' bed while their grandfather stayed up guarding them with a shotgun in hand.
sentences.zh: 斯莱顿兄弟俩经常在外祖父母的床上睡觉，而外祖父则整夜守着他们，手里拿着猎枪。

sentences.en: The brothers eventually returned to school, driven by advice their mum had once given them.
sentences.zh: 兄弟俩最终回到了学校，动力源于母亲曾经给他们的建议。

sentences.en: Keep moving forward and never give up.
sentences.zh: “勇往直前，永不放弃。”

sentences.en: Tim went back to playing football, finding support among his teammates and coach.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆重新开始踢足球，从队友和教练那里得到了支持。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Jeff Slayton faced an entirely new battle.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，杰夫·斯莱顿面临着一场全新的战斗。

sentences.en: You got big arms on you, a detective once told him, before adding, and you're strong enough to put your hands around your mum's neck and kill her.
sentences.zh: “你的胳膊很粗壮，”一名侦探曾对他说，随后补充道，“而且你足够强壮，可以双手掐住你妈妈的脖子杀了她。”

sentences.en: Like his father, Jeff was considered a suspect.
sentences.zh: 像他父亲一样，杰夫也被列为了嫌疑人。

sentences.en: He was the last known person to have seen his mother alive and admitted to having a heated argument with her that evening.
sentences.zh: 他是已知最后见到母亲活着的人，并且承认那天晚上和她发生过激烈的争吵。

sentences.en: Jeff cooperated with authorities, but felt like he was being interrogated all the time.
sentences.zh: 杰夫配合了当局的调查，但感觉自己一直被审讯。

sentences.en: Members of the Lakeland Police Department frequently took him out of school just to question him.
sentences.zh: 莱克兰警察局的人经常把他从学校带走，只为了盘问他。

sentences.en: Jeff voluntarily took a polygraph test, which he passed.
sentences.zh: 杰夫自愿接受了测谎测试，并顺利通过。

sentences.en: When the police wanted to perform the test again and floated the idea of putting Jeff under hypnosis, his grandparents stepped in and said, enough.
sentences.zh: 当警方想再次进行测试，并提出让杰夫接受催眠的想法时，他的外祖父母站出来说：“够了。”

sentences.en: They told investigators to leave Jeff and their family alone and find their daughter's real killer.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉调查人员，别再骚扰杰夫和他们的家人，去找出杀害他们女儿的真正凶手。

sentences.en: Being treated as a suspect caused the grief-stricken Jeff even more agony.
sentences.zh: 被当作嫌疑人对待，让沉浸在悲痛中的杰夫更加痛苦。

sentences.en: Still, he ultimately agreed to sit the second polygraph teSt.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他最终还是同意参加了第二次测谎测试。

sentences.en: Once again, he passed.
sentences.zh: 他再次通过了。

sentences.en: While police accepted there was nothing further implicating him, he remained under a cloud of suspicion.
sentences.zh: 虽然警方承认没有进一步的证据指向他，但他依然笼罩在怀疑的阴影下。

sentences.en: The pressure took its toll.
sentences.zh: 这种压力造成了严重后果。

sentences.en: Both Jeff and Tim dropped out of school, feeling aimless and indifferent.
sentences.zh: 杰夫和蒂姆最终都辍学了，感到漫无目的，对一切都漠不关心。

sentences.en: Jeff fell into a deep depression, during which he contemplated suicide.
sentences.zh: 杰夫陷入了深深的抑郁，期间他曾想过自杀。

sentences.en: The pair obsessively checked the news, hoping to hear of a breakthrough in their mother's case.
sentences.zh: 这对兄弟疯狂地查看新闻，希望能听到母亲案件有突破性进展的消息。

sentences.en: Yet, there was none.
sentences.zh: 然而，什么都没有。

sentences.en: Every person the police interviewed had their hand and footprints compared to those from the crime scene.
sentences.zh: 警方采访过的每一个人，都将其手印和脚印与犯罪现场提取到的进行了比对。

sentences.en: None were a match, and the Slayton case inevitably went cold.
sentences.zh: 结果都不匹配，斯莱顿案最终成了悬案。

sentences.en: Casefile will be back shortly.
sentences.zh: 《案件档案》稍后回来。

sentences.en: Thank you for supporting us by listening to this episode's sponsors.
sentences.zh: 感谢您收听本期节目的赞助商广告，以此支持我们。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening to this episode's ads.
sentences.zh: 感谢您收听本期节目的广告。

sentences.en: By supporting our sponsors, you support Casefile to continue to deliver quality content.
sentences.zh: 通过支持我们的赞助商，您也在支持《案件档案》继续提供优质内容。

sentences.en: Almost 20 years later, in 1998, a Lakeland detective named Brad Grice was tasked with taking a fresh look at the case.
sentences.zh: 近20年后的1998年，一位名叫布拉德·格赖斯的莱克兰侦探受命重新调查此案。

sentences.en: He told the Ledger newspaper,
sentences.zh: 他告诉《莱杰报》：

sentences.en: They say a lot of times in a case like this, it's someone close to you who did it.
sentences.zh: “他们常说，像这样的案件，凶手往往是你身边的人。”

sentences.en: He had the killer's semen sample examined by a crime lab with updated technology, permitting the extraction of a full DNA profile.
sentences.zh: 他让犯罪实验室用更新的技术检测了凶手的精液样本，从而提取出了完整的DNA图谱。

sentences.en: Detective Grice met with Jeff and Tim Slayton, who were now in their 30s.
sentences.zh: 格赖斯侦探会见了当时已三十多岁的杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿。

sentences.en: Both voluntarily provided DNA samples.
sentences.zh: 两人都自愿提供了DNA样本。

sentences.en: Neither matched the killer.
sentences.zh: 结果都与凶手不符。

sentences.en: Jeff Slayton was finally vindicated and officially dismissed as a suspect.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·斯莱顿终于洗清了嫌疑，被正式排除在嫌疑人名单之外。

sentences.en: Linda's ex-husband, Frank Slayton, had cleaned up his life and was no longer drinking, instead committing to repairing his relationship with his sons.
sentences.zh: 琳达的前夫弗兰克·斯莱顿已经改过自新，不再酗酒，转而致力于修复与儿子的关系。

sentences.en: He too gave a DNA sample, which ruled him out of the investigation.
sentences.zh: 他也提供了DNA样本，排除了嫌疑。

sentences.en: Other persons of interest, including Linda's ex-boyfriend, Bobby Dean, were also cleared.
sentences.zh: 包括琳达的前男友鲍比·迪恩在内的其他相关人员也都被排除了嫌疑。

sentences.en: Detective Grice had reached a dead end.
sentences.zh: 格赖斯侦探陷入了死胡同。

sentences.en: Then in September, he received a compelling tip.
sentences.zh: 随后在九月，他收到了一条引人注目的线索。

sentences.en: The year after Linda Slayton was murdered, a 10-year-old Lakeland girl was abducted from her home.
sentences.zh: 在琳达·斯莱顿遇害后的第二年，莱克兰一名10岁女孩在家中被绑架。

sentences.en: The assailant had carried the girl out of her bedroom window where she slept.
sentences.zh: 袭击者从女孩睡觉的卧室窗户将她抱了出去。

sentences.en: He then drove her around for hours, during which she was raped and strangled.
sentences.zh: 随后他开车带着女孩兜了几个小时，期间对她进行了强奸和勒颈。

sentences.en: Her ordeal ended at an interstate overpass.
sentences.zh: 她的苦难在州际公路的一座立交桥上结束了。

sentences.en: Her attacker forced her to climb over the side of the railing.
sentences.zh: 袭击者强迫她爬过护栏边缘。

sentences.en: As she clung desperately onto it, he pried her fingers loose, causing her to fall 24 feet to the ground.
sentences.zh: 当她绝望地抓住护栏时，他掰开了她的手指，导致她从24英尺高处坠落到地面。

sentences.en: She survived and the man responsible was identified as 24-year-old Lakeland local named James Ulmer.
sentences.zh: 她幸存了下来，负责此案的男子被确认为24岁的莱克兰当地人詹姆斯·乌尔默。

sentences.en: He was charged with burglary, kidnapping and attempted murder.
sentences.zh: 他被控入室盗窃、绑架和谋杀未遂。

sentences.en: Ulmer was found to have a history of breaking into people's homes.
sentences.zh: 调查发现乌尔默有闯入民宅的前科。

sentences.en: On one occasion, he was caught standing over a sleeping teenage girl before fleeing.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他被发现站在一名熟睡的少女上方，随后逃离。

sentences.en: It was also believed he was responsible for the death of another girl found dead at the base of an overpass.
sentences.zh: 人们还认为他应对另一名在立交桥底部被发现死亡的女孩负责。

sentences.en: Yet, Ulmer wouldn't cooperate with the investigators.
sentences.zh: 然而，乌尔默拒绝与调查人员合作。

sentences.en: It was discovered that in September 1981,
sentences.zh: 调查发现，1981年9月，

sentences.en: James Ulmer had been staying with a friend who lived in the same apartment complex as Linda Slayton.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·乌尔默曾寄宿在一位朋友家中，该朋友住在琳达·斯莱顿所在的公寓大楼里。

sentences.en: In fact, the apartment was directly across from hers and he was there on the night she was killed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那间公寓就在琳达家正对面，而且在琳达遇害当晚他就在那里。

sentences.en: Given Linda's murder shared striking similarities to Ulmer's known offending,
sentences.zh: 鉴于琳达的谋杀案与乌尔默已知的犯罪手法惊人地相似，

sentences.en: Detective Grice was certain he'd found Linda's killer.
sentences.zh: 格赖斯侦探确信他找到了琳达的凶手。

sentences.en: By the time James Ulmer was on Grice's radar, he had been dead for five years.
sentences.zh: 当詹姆斯·乌尔默进入格赖斯的视线时，他已经死了五年了。

sentences.en: He'd passed away in prison, reportedly from respiratory failure, and had been cremated.
sentences.zh: 他在狱中去世，据报道死于呼吸衰竭，并已被火化。

sentences.en: Further complicating matters was the fact that Ulmer's DNA was never collected and stored when he entered the prison system.
sentences.zh: 更复杂的是，乌尔默进入监狱系统时，从未采集并保存过他的DNA。

sentences.en: Detective Grice spoke with the authorities who'd investigated Ulmer's previous offending.
sentences.zh: 格赖斯侦探与调查过乌尔默先前罪行的当局进行了交谈。

sentences.en: Because that case was closed, everything to do with it, including DNA samples, had been disposed of.
sentences.zh: 由于该案已结案，所有相关资料，包括DNA样本，都已被销毁。

sentences.en: Yet, an opportunity arose when Detective Grice convinced Ulmer's mother to provide him with a DNA sample.
sentences.zh: 然而，当格赖斯侦探说服乌尔默的母亲提供DNA样本时，机会出现了。

sentences.en: It could be used to determine if someone genetically linked to her had raped Linda Slayton.
sentences.zh: 这可以用来确定是否有与她有遗传联系的人强奸了琳达·斯莱顿。

sentences.en: The results concluded that James Ulmer was not Linda's killer.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，詹姆斯·乌尔默不是琳达的凶手。

sentences.en: This was yet another major blow for Detective Grice, who was now back where he started.
sentences.zh: 这对格赖斯侦探来说又是沉重的一击，他现在又回到了原点。

sentences.en: He remained in contact with the Jeff and Tim Slayton, promising them that he wouldn't retire until their mother's killer was caught.
sentences.zh: 他与杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿保持着联系，并向他们保证，在抓到杀害他们母亲的凶手之前，他绝不退休。

sentences.en: He sent the killer's profile to the FBI's National DNA Database, where it was continually compared against new submissions.
sentences.zh: 他将凶手的图谱发送到了联邦调查局的国家DNA数据库，在那里它会不断与新提交的样本进行比对。

sentences.en: But they failed to generate a hit and a reward for information went unclaimed.
sentences.zh: 但他们没能匹配成功，悬赏线索也无人认领。

sentences.en: Detective Grice told the ledger,
sentences.zh: 格赖斯侦探告诉《莱杰报》：

sentences.en: There's still hope, but man, it's tough.
sentences.zh: “希望还在，但伙计，这太难了。”

sentences.en: It's frustrating when you know if you could just identify that DNA.
sentences.zh: “当你明知只要能识别出那份DNA就能破案时，这种感觉真的很令人沮丧。”

sentences.en: It's like having the suspect.
sentences.zh: “就像已经抓到了嫌疑人一样。”

sentences.en: You just don't have the name.
sentences.zh: “只是还不知道名字。”

sentences.en: As years continued to pass,
sentences.zh: 随着岁月流逝，

sentences.en: Detective Grice came to suspect that Linda's killer was likely deceased.
sentences.zh: 格赖斯侦探开始怀疑琳达的凶手可能已经去世了。

sentences.en: After working on the case for 17 years,
sentences.zh: 在处理此案17年后，

sentences.en: Brad Grice retired in 2015 for medical reasons.
sentences.zh: 布拉德·格赖斯于2015年因健康原因退休。

sentences.en: He'd been unable to keep his promise to the Slayton brothers and felt he'd let them down.
sentences.zh: 他没能信守对斯莱顿兄弟的承诺，感到自己辜负了他们。

sentences.en: Although Jeff and Tim were disappointed, they had no hard feelings.
sentences.zh: 尽管杰夫和蒂姆感到失望，但他们并没有怨恨。

sentences.en: They just resigned themselves to the fact that they'd likely take their last breaths without ever knowing who killed their mum.
sentences.zh: 他们只是无奈地接受了一个事实：他们很可能在临终前都无法知道是谁杀害了他们的母亲。

sentences.en: Jeff Slayton, quote,
sentences.zh: 杰夫·斯莱顿说：

sentences.en: It's been rough my whole life not knowing who it is.
sentences.zh: “我这一生都不知道凶手是谁，这种感觉太难受了。”

sentences.en: Always being scared to death I was friends with him.
sentences.zh: “总是害怕得要死，担心自己曾和凶手是朋友。”

sentences.en: Always looking over my shoulder, sleeping with a switchblade knife under my pillow.
sentences.zh: “总是提心吊胆，枕头底下还要藏着一把弹簧刀睡觉。”

sentences.en: Tim Slayton told the Ledger,
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·斯莱顿告诉《莱杰报》：

sentences.en: It could be that guy over there.
sentences.zh: “凶手可能是那边的某个人。”

sentences.en: You just don't know.
sentences.zh: “你根本无从知晓。”

sentences.en: By now, more than two dozen detectives had actively worked on the Slayton case.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，已有超过两打侦探积极参与过斯莱顿案的调查。

sentences.en: Leads were pursued interstate in Louisiana and North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 线索一直追查到路易斯安那州和北卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: Jeff and Tim Slayton continued to visit and call the Lakeland Police Department so the detectives wouldn't forget them.
sentences.zh: 杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿继续拜访并致电莱克兰警察局，以免侦探们忘记他们。

sentences.en: They wound up befriending these officers, who reassured the brothers that they were still very passionate about solving the crime.
sentences.zh: 他们最终与这些警官成了朋友，警官们向兄弟俩保证，他们依然对破案充满热情。

sentences.en: But years continued to slip by with no arrests.
sentences.zh: 但岁月流逝，依然无人被捕。

sentences.en: Hope was fading.
sentences.zh: 希望正在破灭。

sentences.en: In 2018, Parabon Nanolabs, a company that specialises in using genetic genealogy to investigate cold cases, reached out to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.
sentences.zh: 2018年，专门利用遗传家谱调查悬案的公司Parabon Nanolabs联系了佛罗里达州执法局。

sentences.en: They asked if they wanted to send the DNA from the Slayton case for further testing due to the growing success of this new form of investigation.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这种新型调查方式日益成功，他们询问是否可以将斯莱顿案的DNA样本送去进行进一步检测。

sentences.en: 38 years had passed since Linda's murder, but the rape kit had been kept in pristine condition in anticipation for a moment like this.
sentences.zh: 距离琳达遇害已经过去了38年，但强奸取证包一直被完好地保存着，以等待这一刻的到来。

sentences.en: Cece Moore was the head of Parabon Nanolabs' genetic genealogy unit.
sentences.zh: 西西·摩尔是Parabon Nanolabs遗传家谱部门的负责人。

sentences.en: She was an expert in the field, and her team was given the Slayton case file.
sentences.zh: 她是该领域的专家，她的团队接手了斯莱顿案的档案。

sentences.en: They began by uploading the killer's DNA into a public genealogy website called GEDmatch.
sentences.zh: 他们首先将凶手的DNA上传到了一个名为GEDmatch的公共家谱网站。

sentences.en: Customers voluntarily submitted saliva swabs to genealogical testing companies like GEDmatch in exchange for an ancestry report.
sentences.zh: 客户自愿向GEDmatch等家谱检测公司提交唾液拭子，以换取一份祖源报告。

sentences.en: They could then connect with family members and distant relatives via online databases.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们可以通过在线数据库与家庭成员和远房亲戚建立联系。

sentences.en: Similarly, cold case investigators uploaded anonymous DNA from crime scenes to the same databases, but with the intention of identifying suspects through their familial lineage.
sentences.zh: 同样，悬案调查人员也会将犯罪现场的匿名DNA上传到这些数据库，目的是通过血缘关系识别嫌疑人。

sentences.en: This method was used to help capture the Golden State killer a year prior, as covered in episode 53 of Case File.
sentences.zh: 这种方法曾用于协助抓获“金州杀手”，《案件档案》第53期曾对此进行过报道。

sentences.en: Unsurprisingly, Linda Slayton's killer hadn't uploaded his DNA to GEDmatch.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，琳达·斯莱顿的凶手并没有将自己的DNA上传到GEDmatch。

sentences.en: But genealogist Cece Moore and her team constructed a family tree based on his distant relatives who had.
sentences.zh: 但家谱学家西西·摩尔和她的团队根据上传过DNA的远房亲戚构建了一棵家谱树。

sentences.en: They filled in the gaps using birth certificates, marriage licences, obituaries, and social media.
sentences.zh: 他们利用出生证明、结婚证、讣告和社交媒体填补了空白。

sentences.en: It only took Moore's team a weekend to uncover three genetic networks, individual branches that converged into one single family.
sentences.zh: 摩尔的团队仅用了一个周末就发现了三个遗传网络，即汇聚成同一个家族的各个分支。

sentences.en: The family only had one son, and he had roots in Lakeland in 1981.
sentences.zh: 这个家庭只有一个儿子，而且他在1981年时在莱克兰有生活轨迹。

sentences.en: Cece Moore was highly confident he was the DNA contributor.
sentences.zh: 西西·摩尔非常确信他就是DNA贡献者。

sentences.en: Tim Slayton's favourite sport was American football.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·斯莱顿最喜欢的运动是美式橄榄球。

sentences.en: Weeks after his mother was killed, 14-year-old Tim returned to the game, finding comfort among his teammates.
sentences.zh: 母亲遇害几周后，14岁的蒂姆回到了赛场，在队友中找到了慰藉。

sentences.en: One of his biggest supporters was his team's assistant coach, a 20-year-old man affectionately called Coach Joe.
sentences.zh: 他最大的支持者之一是球队的助理教练，一个被亲切地称为“乔教练”的20岁年轻人。

sentences.en: Coach Joe's full name was Joseph Mills.
sentences.zh: 乔教练的全名是约瑟夫·米尔斯。

sentences.en: When he wasn't volunteering with Lakeland's youth football program,
sentences.zh: 当他不参与莱克兰青年橄榄球项目的志愿服务时，

sentences.en: Mills worked at a dairy warehouse.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯在一家乳制品仓库工作。

sentences.en: He knew Linda Slayton was a single mum who couldn't afford a car and helped her out by giving Tim rides to and from practice.
sentences.zh: 他知道琳达·斯莱顿是一位买不起车的单身母亲，于是通过接送蒂姆往返训练场来帮助她。

sentences.en: In fact, he had picked up Tim and driven him home on the very day Linda Slayton was later killed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在琳达·斯莱顿遇害的那天，他还接了蒂姆并开车送他回家。

sentences.en: The next day, police interviewed Mills briefly over the phone.
sentences.zh: 第二天，警方通过电话简短地采访了米尔斯。

sentences.en: He wasn't questioned any further, meaning he'd failed to register on their radar.
sentences.zh: 他没有受到进一步盘问，这意味着他没能进入警方的视线。

sentences.en: It wouldn't have helped that those who knew him would have provided glowing character references.
sentences.zh: 那些认识他的人提供的溢美之词对他来说也起到了掩护作用。

sentences.en: When genealogist Cece Moore was tracing Linda Slayton's killer in 2019, all branches led to Joseph Mills.
sentences.zh: 当家谱学家西西·摩尔在2019年追踪琳达·斯莱顿的凶手时，所有线索都指向了约瑟夫·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Better yet, he was still alive.
sentences.zh: 更好的是，他还活着。

sentences.en: The now 58-year-old lived on Bailey Road, 30 minutes from the crime scene.
sentences.zh: 现年58岁的他住在距离案发现场30分钟路程的贝利路上。

sentences.en: It was the same place he'd lived in 1981.
sentences.zh: 那正是他1981年居住的地方。

sentences.en: Mills had changed a lot since then.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯自那时起发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: He'd gone bald and his facial hair had grayed.
sentences.zh: 他秃了头，胡子也花白了。

sentences.en: He was still married to the same woman and not only did he have children of his own, but grandchildren as well.
sentences.zh: 他依然与同一个女人结婚，不仅有了自己的孩子，还有了孙辈。

sentences.en: Over the past three decades, Mills had taken on a variety of jobs.
sentences.zh: 在过去的三十年里，米尔斯从事过各种工作。

sentences.en: Now he was running his own cleaning business.
sentences.zh: 现在他经营着自己的清洁公司。

sentences.en: Mills was also known to police.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯也曾被警方注意过。

sentences.en: In 1984, he had been convicted of grand theft after forging a will.
sentences.zh: 1984年，他因伪造遗嘱被判犯有重大盗窃罪。

sentences.en: He didn't go to prison, but his handprints were taken and kept on file.
sentences.zh: 他没有坐牢，但留下了手印并被存档。

sentences.en: These were compared to the partial palm print lifted from Linda Slayton's windowsill.
sentences.zh: 这些手印与从琳达·斯莱顿窗台上提取到的部分掌纹进行了比对。

sentences.en: It was a match.
sentences.zh: 匹配成功。

sentences.en: The final piece of the puzzle was comparing Joseph Mills' DNA to that of Linda's killer.
sentences.zh: 拼图的最后一块是将约瑟夫·米尔斯的DNA与琳达凶手的DNA进行比对。

sentences.en: Investigators covertly surveilled Mills for several weekends, waiting for an opportunity to discreetly obtain a sample of his DNA.
sentences.zh: 调查人员秘密监视了米尔斯几个周末，等待机会悄悄获取他的DNA样本。

sentences.en: This would be done by picking up something he discarded, like a tissue or coffee cup.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过捡拾他丢弃的东西来实现，比如纸巾或咖啡杯。

sentences.en: When this approach failed, investigators secretly seized Mills' trash from the curb outside his home.
sentences.zh: 当这种方法失败后，调查人员秘密扣押了米尔斯家路边的垃圾。

sentences.en: After digging through the garbage bags, they uncovered a piece of used medical adhesive tape for a colostomy back.
sentences.zh: 在翻找垃圾袋后，他们发现了一块用过的医用胶带，用于固定造口袋。

sentences.en: A 2013 photograph on Mills' Facebook page showed he had a colostomy back.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯Facebook页面上2013年的一张照片显示他装有造口袋。

sentences.en: The tape was most certainly his, but to be sure, officers also collected two cotton swabs and a plastic spoon from the trash.
sentences.zh: 胶带几乎肯定属于他，但为了保险起见，警官还从垃圾中收集了两根棉签和一把塑料勺子。

sentences.en: All the items were sent off for testing.
sentences.zh: 所有物品都被送去检测。

sentences.en: Eleven days later, the results were in.
sentences.zh: 十一天后，结果出来了。

sentences.en: Joseph Mills' DNA matched the DNA of Linda Slayton's killer.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·米尔斯的DNA与琳达·斯莱顿凶手的DNA相符。

sentences.en: Following this, police spoke with the Joseph Mills at his home.
sentences.zh: 随后，警方在他家中与约瑟夫·米尔斯进行了谈话。

sentences.en: He said he didn't remember Linda Slayton or her murder.
sentences.zh: 他说他不记得琳达·斯莱顿或她的谋杀案了。

sentences.en: He was then shown photographs of Linda and her two sons.
sentences.zh: 随后向他展示了琳达和她两个儿子的照片。

sentences.en: This prompted Mills to claim he did remember them, but hadn't known Linda personally.
sentences.zh: 这促使米尔斯改口称他确实记得他们，但并不认识琳达本人。

sentences.en: He also said that he didn't recall coaching Tim Slayton or that he'd dropped him off at the Slayton's home the night Linda was killed.
sentences.zh: 他还说他不记得曾担任过蒂姆·斯莱顿的教练，也不记得在琳达遇害当晚送他回过斯莱顿家。

sentences.en: Eight days later, on Thursday December 12, 2019, police met with Mills again and placed him under arreSt.
sentences.zh: 八天后的2019年12月12日星期四，警方再次会见米尔斯并将其逮捕。

sentences.en: He didn't seem surprised and never asked why.
sentences.zh: 他似乎并不惊讶，也从未问过原因。

sentences.en: Instead, he was unusually calm and showed no emotion.
sentences.zh: 相反，他异常冷静，没有任何情绪波动。

sentences.en: During a subsequent police interview, Mills was now willing to open up about his history with Tim Slayton.
sentences.zh: 在随后的警方审讯中，米尔斯终于愿意敞开心扉谈论他与蒂姆·斯莱顿的过往。

sentences.en: He asserted that whenever he dropped Tim off at home after practice, he stayed in his car.
sentences.zh: 他坚称每次训练结束后送蒂姆回家时，他都待在车里。

sentences.en: Mills maintained that he had never been inside the Slayton home at any time, for any reason.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯坚持说他从未在任何时间、以任何理由进入过斯莱顿家。

sentences.en: What we have tells us a different story, a detective responded, before adding,
sentences.zh: “我们掌握的情况告诉我们的是另一个故事，”一名侦探回应道，随后补充说：

sentences.en: You were in that apartment.
sentences.zh: “你进过那间公寓。”

sentences.en: Mills was informed that evidence placed him in Linda Slayton's bedroom, with one detective remarking,
sentences.zh: 米尔斯被告知证据显示他曾出现在琳达·斯莱顿的卧室里，一名侦探评论道：

sentences.en: It's been 38 years and I'm sure you go to bed every night thinking about this.
sentences.zh: “已经过去38年了，我相信你每天晚上睡觉时都会想到这件事。”

sentences.en: Mills remained indignant, reiterating that he had never been inside the apartment.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯依然愤愤不平，重申他从未进入过那间公寓。

sentences.en: Upon learning that his handprints and DNA were found at the crime scene, Mills changed his story again.
sentences.zh: 当得知他的手印和DNA在犯罪现场被发现后，米尔斯再次改变了说法。

sentences.en: He said that he had met Linda for the first time on Thursday September 3, 1981, when he dropped Tim home.
sentences.zh: 他说他是在1981年9月3日星期四送蒂姆回家时第一次见到琳达的。

sentences.en: Linda approached Mills' car to thank him.
sentences.zh: 琳达走到米尔斯的车前向他道谢。

sentences.en: According to Mills, Linda gave him an open invitation to stop by for, quote,
sentences.zh: 据米尔斯所说，琳达当时主动邀请他去家里坐坐，用他的话说：

sentences.en: A good time.
sentences.zh: “共度良宵。”

sentences.en: Mills took her up on her offer that night.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯当晚就接受了她的邀请。

sentences.en: He entered her bedroom through her unlocked window.
sentences.zh: 他通过没锁的窗户进入了她的卧室。

sentences.en: Linda was lying on her bed waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 琳达当时正躺在床上等他。

sentences.en: Mills claimed that the wire coat hanger was already around her neck and she asked him to tighten it for her pleasure.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯声称，那个金属衣架当时已经套在她的脖子上了，是她要求他勒紧衣架以寻求快感。

sentences.en: They had consensual sex that Mills described as wild, during which he twisted the wire tighter and tighter as per Linda's wishes.
sentences.zh: 他们发生了双方自愿的性行为，米尔斯形容过程非常狂野，期间他按照琳达的要求，将衣架越勒越紧。

sentences.en: Linda then lost consciousness.
sentences.zh: 随后琳达失去了知觉。

sentences.en: After finishing, Mills left back out the window without checking to see if Linda had woken up.
sentences.zh: 事后，米尔斯从窗户原路离开，并没有查看琳达是否醒来。

sentences.en: He claimed that he'd only learnt that she'd died when detectives questioned him about it later.
sentences.zh: 他声称直到后来侦探审问他时，他才知道琳达已经死了。

sentences.en: Linda's autopsy results determined her injuries were inconsistent with consensual sex.
sentences.zh: 琳达的尸检结果显示，她所受的伤与双方自愿的性行为不符。

sentences.en: There were even self-sustained claw marks to her neck consistent with her struggling to remove the wire.
sentences.zh: 她的脖子上甚至有她自己抓挠留下的痕迹，这表明她当时曾挣扎着想要取下衣架。

sentences.en: When detectives pointed out how deep the hanger was embedded in Linda's skin, Mills maintained, quote,
sentences.zh: 当侦探指出衣架嵌入琳达皮肤有多深时，米尔斯依然坚称，引用他的话：

sentences.en: It was a game.
sentences.zh: “那只是个游戏。”

sentences.en: Detectives were unconvinced.
sentences.zh: 侦探们并不相信。

sentences.en: They were certain that after dropping Tim Slayton home, Joseph Mills returned to the apartment later, having made the decision to rape Linda.
sentences.zh: 他们确信，在送蒂姆·斯莱顿回家后，约瑟夫·米尔斯又回到了公寓，并决定强奸琳达。

sentences.en: He broke in through her bedroom window at around 9pm during a brief period of time when no one was home.
sentences.zh: 晚上9点左右，趁家中无人，他从卧室窗户闯入。

sentences.en: Mills then lay in wait in Linda's bedroom, likely hiding in the closet, where he collected the wire hanger.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯随后潜伏在琳达的卧室里，很可能躲在衣柜中，并在那里拿到了那个金属衣架。

sentences.en: When Linda retired for bed that night, she walked into her room and closed the door, oblivious that Mills was already in there waiting for her.
sentences.zh: 当晚琳达回房休息时，她走进房间并关上了门，完全不知道米尔斯已经躲在里面等着她了。

sentences.en: Joseph Mills was charged with burglary, sexual battery and first-degree murder.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·米尔斯被控入室盗窃、性侵犯和一级谋杀罪。

sentences.en: Jeff and Tim Slayton were stunned to learn a trusted family friend had killed their mother.
sentences.zh: 杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿得知杀害他们母亲的竟是深受信赖的家庭朋友时，感到震惊不已。

sentences.en: The thought that Coach Joe could be responsible had never even crossed their minds.
sentences.zh: 他们从未想过乔教练竟然会是凶手。

sentences.en: They hoped to see Mills face trial, explain himself on the stand and face the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 他们希望看到米尔斯接受审判，在证人席上为自己辩解，并被判处死刑。

sentences.en: After being advised by his attorney that it was in his best interest to plead guilty to all charges, Mills did so.
sentences.zh: 在律师建议认罪对自身最有利后，米尔斯选择了认罪。

sentences.en: Yet, he still refused to admit to killing Linda Slayton.
sentences.zh: 然而，他依然拒绝承认杀害了琳达·斯莱顿。

sentences.en: Jeff and Tim Slayton were in court during sentencing in February 2022, surrounded by supportive friends and family.
sentences.zh: 2022年2月，杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿在亲友的支持下出席了量刑听证会。

sentences.en: They were both given the opportunity to speak.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都有机会发言。

sentences.en: Jeff turned to Mills and tearfully asked over and over, sometimes yelling,
sentences.zh: 杰夫转向米尔斯，含泪反复质问，有时甚至大声吼道：

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: “为什么？”

sentences.en: I just want to know why, Joe.
sentences.zh: “我只想知道为什么，乔。”

sentences.en: Why'd you take my mama from me?
sentences.zh: “你为什么要夺走我的妈妈？”

sentences.en: I loved my mama.
sentences.zh: “我爱我的妈妈。”

sentences.en: We were happy.
sentences.zh: “我们曾经很幸福。”

sentences.en: I hate you.
sentences.zh: “我恨你。”

sentences.en: You can't die and burn in hell fast enough for me.
sentences.zh: “就算你死后在地狱里受尽折磨，也难消我心头之恨。”

sentences.en: Mills remained silent and stone-faced in response.
sentences.zh: 米尔斯对此保持沉默，面无表情。

sentences.en: Linda's sister, Judy Butler, was met with the same reaction when she asked Mills,
sentences.zh: 琳达的妹妹朱迪·巴特勒在质问米尔斯时也得到了同样的反应：

sentences.en: Do you have any soul?
sentences.zh: “你还有良心吗？”

sentences.en: Do you have any remorse?
sentences.zh: “你有一丝悔意吗？”

sentences.en: The court also heard from Linda's grandchildren, who never got to meet her.
sentences.zh: 法庭还听取了琳达从未谋面的孙辈们的陈述。

sentences.en: When the defendant was given the chance to speak, he told the court,
sentences.zh: 当被告有机会发言时，他告诉法庭：

sentences.en: I am a good person.
sentences.zh: “我是一个好人。”

sentences.en: I'm not that person that they're painting me out to be.
sentences.zh: “我不是他们所描述的那种人。”

sentences.en: He explained that he owned a successful business.
sentences.zh: 他解释说自己经营着一家成功的企业。

sentences.en: The judge was unmoved by these claiMs.
sentences.zh: 法官对这些辩解无动于衷。

sentences.en: He sentenced Joseph Mills to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
sentences.zh: 他判处约瑟夫·米尔斯终身监禁，不得假释。

sentences.en: A tearful Jeff Slayton told the media outside court,
sentences.zh: 杰夫·斯莱顿在庭外含泪告诉媒体：

sentences.en: I don't know if there's anything such as closure, but it has been easier knowing he's locked up.
sentences.zh: “我不知道这世上是否真的有‘了结’这回事，但知道他被关起来了，心里确实好受了一些。”

sentences.en: Tim Slayton added,
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·斯莱顿补充道：

sentences.en: It's not over in the sense, cause he's still walking, and my mum's not.
sentences.zh: “这还没结束，因为他还活着，而我的母亲却不在了。”

sentences.en: Detective Brad Grice was one of the dozens of detectives who investigated the Slayton case over the near 40 years it went unsolved.
sentences.zh: 布拉德·格赖斯侦探是近40年来调查斯莱顿案的数十名侦探之一，该案长期未破。

sentences.en: He had worked on it for 17 of those years, but had to retire before it was solved.
sentences.zh: 他参与调查了17年，但在案件告破前不得不退休。

sentences.en: When Joseph Mills was identified as the killer, Detective Grice blamed himself for not having identified him sooner.
sentences.zh: 当约瑟夫·米尔斯被确认为凶手时，格赖斯侦探自责没能早点查出他。

sentences.en: The Slayton brothers felt differently.
sentences.zh: 斯莱顿兄弟的看法则不同。

sentences.en: They expressed gratitude to all those who worked to find their mother's killer, including Detective Grice, whom they considered a friend.
sentences.zh: 他们向所有致力于寻找杀害母亲凶手的人表达了感激，包括他们视为朋友的格赖斯侦探。

sentences.en: In fact, Jeff was so appreciative of the detective's effort, he named one of his sons after him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，杰夫非常感激这位侦探的付出，甚至用他的名字为自己的一个儿子命名。

sentences.en: The Slayton brothers held the same regard for Sergeant Edgar Pickett, who uncovered the killer's palm print on Linda's bedroom windowsill.
sentences.zh: 斯莱顿兄弟对埃德加·皮克特警官也怀有同样的敬意，正是他发现了凶手在琳达卧室窗台上留下的掌纹。

sentences.en: This evidence helped solidify Joseph Mills' guilt.
sentences.zh: 这一证据有力地证实了约瑟夫·米尔斯的罪行。

sentences.en: By the time Jeff and Tim were able to meet Pickett and thank him, he was 94 years old.
sentences.zh: 当杰夫和蒂姆见到皮克特并向他致谢时，他已经94岁了。

sentences.en: It was a case Pickett had never forgotten.
sentences.zh: 这是一个皮克特从未忘记的案件。

sentences.en: Once his job at the crime scene was over, his mind kept returning to the two Slayton boys.
sentences.zh: 当他在犯罪现场的工作结束后，他的思绪总是回到那两个斯莱顿男孩身上。

sentences.en: Pickett himself had children and was driven to solve Linda's murder to give her sons closure.
sentences.zh: 皮克特自己也有孩子，他破获琳达谋杀案的动力就是为了给她的儿子们一个交代。

sentences.en: Despite his involvement in the investigation, Pickett had never heard the name Joseph Mills and was unaware that the young man had been questioned early on in the investigation.
sentences.zh: 尽管参与了调查，皮克特从未听说过约瑟夫·米尔斯这个名字，也不知道这个年轻人早在调查初期就曾被问话。

sentences.en: In fact, Pickett revealed that he had been told to compare the palm print to a number of black men following reports of suspicious activity by black individuals at the time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，皮克特透露，当时由于有关于黑人可疑活动的报告，他被告知将掌纹与多名黑人进行比对。

sentences.en: Pickett, who was African-American himself, admitted that the prejudice of his white colleagues influenced his own mindset.
sentences.zh: 身为非裔美国人的皮克特承认，他白人同事的偏见影响了他自己的思维方式。

sentences.en: Random black men were questioned and fingerprinted en masse.
sentences.zh: 当时，随机的黑人男性被大规模地传唤并采集指纹。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the white football coach who'd been at the Slayton home the night Linda was murdered was completely overlooked.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，那个在琳达遇害当晚曾出现在斯莱顿家的白人橄榄球教练却被完全忽略了。

sentences.en: Pickett admitted that he didn't handle the case like he should have and it had been on his conscience ever since.
sentences.zh: 皮克特承认他处理此案的方式有误，这让他一直心存愧疚。

sentences.en: Despite this, case detectives maintained that Joseph Mills didn't slip through the cracks.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，负责案件的侦探们坚称约瑟夫·米尔斯并没有被漏掉。

sentences.en: Genealogist C.C.
sentences.zh: 基因学家C.C.

sentences.en: Moore, who had worked on hundreds of cases and solved more than 50 using genetic genealogy,
sentences.zh: 摩尔曾处理过数百起案件，并利用遗传系谱学解决了50多起案件，

sentences.en: said that Linda Slayton's made her the angriest because the killer targeted Linda while her children slept nearby.
sentences.zh: 她说琳达·斯莱顿的案子让她最愤怒，因为凶手在琳达的孩子就在附近睡觉时对她下了毒手。

sentences.en: When Joseph Mills blamed Linda, denigrating her and making her look bad in front of her own children, Moore's disgust grew further.
sentences.zh: 当约瑟夫·米尔斯指责琳达，在她的孩子面前诋毁她、抹黑她时，摩尔感到更加厌恶。

sentences.en: C.C.
sentences.zh: C.C.

sentences.en: Moore expressed gratitude to the original crime scene investigators, saying,
sentences.zh: 摩尔对最初的犯罪现场调查人员表示了感谢，她说：

sentences.en: At the time this crime was committed, they didn't even know DNA was going to be used in criminal investigations.
sentences.zh: “在犯罪发生时，他们甚至不知道DNA会被用于刑事调查。”

sentences.en: And so the fact that they collected that and then it was stored responsibly and carefully all these years by that department is so important.
sentences.zh: “因此，他们收集了这些证据，并且多年来由该部门负责任地妥善保存，这一点至关重要。”

sentences.en: If that hadn't happened, we couldn't have done our work.
sentences.zh: “如果不是这样，我们就不可能完成我们的工作。”

sentences.en: In May 2019, GEDmatch, the DNA database used to help solve the Slayton case, changed its privacy rules.
sentences.zh: 2019年5月，用于协助侦破斯莱顿案的DNA数据库GEDmatch更改了其隐私规则。

sentences.en: It is now much more difficult to solve cold cases using this method.
sentences.zh: 现在，利用这种方法侦破悬案变得困难多了。

sentences.zh: C.C.

sentences.en: Moore said,
sentences.zh: 摩尔说：

sentences.en: Whatever one thinks about this decision, it is inarguably a setback for justice, victims, and their families.
sentences.zh: “无论人们对这一决定有何看法，这无疑是对正义、受害者及其家属的一次挫折。”

sentences.en: Jeff and Tim Slayton have come to terms with the Joseph Mills' outcome, but still lack closure.
sentences.zh: 杰夫和蒂姆·斯莱顿已经接受了约瑟夫·米尔斯案的结果，但仍感到无法释怀。

sentences.en: It stung them that he was able to live a full life and raise a family for four decades.
sentences.zh: 让他们感到痛苦的是，他竟然能逍遥法外四十年，过着正常的生活并养育家庭。

sentences.en: The brothers felt they were handed a far harsher sentence than he was, as they had to grow up and live without their mother.
sentences.zh: 兄弟俩觉得他们受到的惩罚比他严厉得多，因为他们必须在没有母亲的情况下长大成人。

sentences.en: Still, they harboured no resentment towards law enforcement for taking so long to apprehend Mills, with Tim Slayton explaining,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他们对执法部门花了这么长时间才逮捕米尔斯并没有怨恨，蒂姆·斯莱顿解释说：

sentences.en: I know it's a lot of hard work behind the scenes that people don't see that goes on.
sentences.zh: “我知道幕后有很多人们看不到的艰苦工作。”

sentences.en: You know, what they do, the hours upon hours they put in.
sentences.zh: “你知道，他们所做的，他们投入的无数个小时。”

sentences.en: I mean, you could get mad, but only so much could be done in a day.
sentences.zh: “我的意思是，你可能会生气，但一天之内能做的事情毕竟有限。”

sentences.en: The brothers have said that they couldn't have survived their ordeal without each other.
sentences.zh: 兄弟俩说，如果没有彼此，他们无法熬过那段苦难。

sentences.en: Over the years, they stayed close, living just a few miles apart and sharing the same hobbies so they could constantly be in each other's lives.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们一直保持亲密，住得相距仅几英里，并分享同样的爱好，以便能时刻参与对方的生活。

sentences.en: They visited their mother's graveside often and lit a candle every year on the anniversary of her murder.
sentences.zh: 他们经常去母亲的墓前祭扫，并在她遇害的周年纪念日每年点燃一支蜡烛。

sentences.en: Jeff Slayton, quote,
sentences.zh: 杰夫·斯莱顿引用他母亲的话说：

sentences.en: My mum, she's looking down on us and would want us to live our lives and do good.
sentences.zh: “我的妈妈，她在天之灵看着我们，她会希望我们好好生活，多做善事。”

sentences.en: I want to make her proud.
sentences.zh: “我想让她为我感到骄傲。”

sentences.en: After his mother's murder, Tim Slayton cried for two weeks straight.
sentences.zh: 母亲遇害后，蒂姆·斯莱顿连续哭了两个星期。

sentences.en: Then he stopped and has been unable to cry since.
sentences.zh: 然后他停了下来，从此再也哭不出来了。

sentences.en: Some have seen his inability to cry as cold, but it's as though Tim ran out of tears.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为他哭不出来是因为冷漠，但其实就像是蒂姆的眼泪已经流干了。

sentences.en: Following Linda's death, Joseph Mills continued to act as a friend to Tim.
sentences.zh: 琳达死后，约瑟夫·米尔斯继续扮演蒂姆的朋友。

sentences.en: He continued picking him up and dropping him off at football practice.
sentences.zh: 他继续接送他去参加橄榄球训练。

sentences.en: During these trips, Mills asked about Linda's case and what leads police were looking into.
sentences.zh: 在这些行程中，米尔斯会询问琳达案件的情况以及警方正在调查的线索。

sentences.en: Tim didn't know it at the time, but his mum's killer was using him to scope out the ongoing investigation.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆当时并不知道，他母亲的凶手正在利用他来打探调查进展。

sentences.en: Then, a month after Linda's murder, Mills had a team photo taken.
sentences.zh: 后来，在琳达遇害一个月后，米尔斯拍了一张球队合影。

sentences.en: In it, Tim and his teammates stand side by side in their white jerseys.
sentences.zh: 照片里，蒂姆和队友们穿着白色球衣并排站着。

sentences.en: Directly behind Tim was Coach Joe.
sentences.zh: 在蒂姆的正后方就是乔教练。

sentences.en: Tim saw his coach organising this as a show of solidarity and support.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆当时认为教练组织这次拍照是为了表达团结和支持。

sentences.en: He appreciated the photo so much that he hung it up in his bedroom at his grandparents' home.
sentences.zh: 他非常珍视这张照片，把它挂在祖父母家卧室的墙上。

sentences.en: He had no clue that he was looking at the face of his mother's killer daily.
sentences.zh: 他根本不知道，他每天都在看着杀害他母亲的凶手的脸。

sentences.en: The photo was once a source of pride for Tim, but now it disgusts him.
sentences.zh: 这张照片曾经是蒂姆的骄傲，但现在却让他感到恶心。

sentences.en: He sees it as proof of how cold-hearted Joseph Mills was.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为约瑟夫·米尔斯冷酷无情的证据。

sentences.en: Worse still were the haunting memories of seeing his mother's brutalised and naked body in situ.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，亲眼目睹母亲惨遭蹂躏的赤裸尸体，那段记忆一直挥之不去。

sentences.en: Tim Slayton, quote,
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·斯莱顿引用他的话：

sentences.en: I've seen the crime scene.
sentences.zh: “我见过犯罪现场。”

sentences.en: It's in my head every day.
sentences.zh: “它每天都在我脑海里。”

sentences.en: I've got to live with that.
sentences.zh: “我必须带着这种记忆生活。”

sentences.en: Unlike his younger brother, Jeff Slayton cries all the time.
sentences.zh: 与弟弟不同，杰夫·斯莱顿总是哭个不停。

sentences.en: He tells himself he won't, but tears fall whenever he starts thinking about his mother.
sentences.zh: 他告诉自己不要哭，但每当想起母亲，泪水就会夺眶而出。

sentences.en: Speaking with the journalist Paul Lazarn about Joseph Mills, Jeff said tearfully,
sentences.zh: 在与记者保罗·拉扎恩谈论约瑟夫·米尔斯时，杰夫含泪说道：

sentences.en: The day he murdered my mum, he murdered my childhood.
sentences.zh: “他谋杀我母亲的那一天，也谋杀了我的童年。”

sentences.en: It was the last day me and my brother were kids.
sentences.zh: “那是我和我弟弟作为孩子度过的最后一天。”

sentences.en: Jeff harbours immense guilt, telling filmmakers of the CBS series The Betrayal of Linda Slayton,
sentences.zh: 杰夫怀有巨大的负罪感，他告诉CBS系列纪录片《琳达·斯莱顿的背叛》的制作人：

sentences.en: In order to explain why he and Tim didn't hear the attack, Jeff believes that Joseph Mills threatened their mother to keep quiet or else he'd hurt her children.
sentences.zh: 为了解释为什么他和蒂姆没有听到袭击声，杰夫认为约瑟夫·米尔斯当时威胁了他们的母亲，如果不保持安静就会伤害她的孩子。

sentences.en: Jeff Slayton, quote,
sentences.zh: 杰夫·斯莱顿引用他的话：

sentences.en: So, she saved us, is the way we look at it.
sentences.zh: “所以，我们认为她是救了我们。”

sentences.en: She could have screamed and yelled, like a lot of people would have done if you're in that position.
sentences.zh: “她本可以尖叫和大喊，就像很多人在那种情况下会做的那样。”

sentences.en: But again, she was looking out for us.
sentences.zh: “但话说回来，她是在保护我们。”

sentences.en: That was probably the last thing on her mind.
sentences.zh: “那可能是她脑海中最后想的事情。”

sentences.en: Was us.
sentences.zh: “就是我们。”
